items.title: Wilson "Chembo" Corniel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019
items.q: then I landed a gig with one of the top bands, when I was young, in 1977 Bobby Rodriguez Y La Compania we were like a band of kids

ctx.x: Oh yes. Oh yes definitely. You know because when I was a kid trying to find information we didn’t have YouTube, we didn’t have the internet. I had my album, I’d put on a record and I would hear the conga player but you would hear the dominant hand and you didn’t know what the left hand was doing so therefore you were doing it wrong because you had

to see that there’s a certain technique that fills in the whole pattern of a tumbao. All you hear is [scats] see that’s the right hand only. But what’s this one doing? There’s another, there’s the other half that you’re learning. So you start picking up bad habits already until somebody who knows, and I got in contact with these people that moved in my neighborhood, professional percussionists that were playing with Eddie Palmieri in the 70s, and they seen that I had a little bit of talent so they took me up and…
Were your parents supportive of your musical path?
